About Ocean Springs

Living in Ocean Springs

Ocean Springs is across Biloxi Bay from Biloxi, in Jackson County. The French built Fort Maurepas here in 1699, one of the first European settlements on the Gulf Coast. Today the downtown along Washington Avenue and Government Street is known for restaurants, shops and the arts.

Neighborhoods range from older streets near downtown and Front Beach to newer subdivisions toward Interstate 10 and the Gulf Park Estates area.

Places to know

Around Ocean Springs

  • Downtown Ocean SpringsRestaurants, shops and live music along Washington Avenue and Government Street.
  • Walter Anderson Museum of ArtMuseum dedicated to the Ocean Springs artist Walter Anderson.
  • Peter Anderson Arts & Crafts FestivalLarge outdoor arts festival held downtown each November.
  • Gulf Islands National Seashore, Davis BayouNational park area with trails, a visitor center and a boat launch.
  • Front BeachBeach and harbor along Biloxi Bay.

Getting around

Roads and commute

US 90 crosses the Biloxi Bay Bridge west to Biloxi, Interstate 10 runs north of town, and Keesler Air Force Base and the Ingalls shipyard in Pascagoula are both a short drive.

Workers who live in Ocean Springs spend an average of 26.3 minutes getting to work, one way (Mississippi average: 25.6).

Near the water

Flood zones and insurance costs can change from one street to the next on the Coast. Look up any address on FEMA's flood map, and ask me for help getting insurance quotes before you make an offer.
